subject.title: [Feature]: Per-user heartbeat routing for channel-level heartbeat messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a channel-level WhatsApp heartbeat recipient contract for HEARTBEAT_OK acknowledgments, and if so what field shape and validation policy should it use?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-proven, but adding `channels.whatsapp.heartbeat.target` or `targets` creates a new compatibility-sensitive config surface and must define OK-only semantics, per-account precedence, and allowlist/pairing validation before implementation.

options.title: Add OK-only targets
options.body: Add a narrow `channels.whatsapp.heartbeat.targets` style contract for visible OK acknowledgments only, with account/allowlist validation and unchanged alert routing.

options.title: Use existing agent heartbeat routing
options.body: Reject channel-level recipients and document `agents.*.heartbeat.target`/`to` as the supported whole-delivery workaround, accepting that OK and alert routing remain coupled.

options.title: Design a generic channel recipient policy
options.body: Pause this issue in favor of a broader cross-channel heartbeat recipient design if maintainers want the same contract for multiple channels.

recommendation.title: Add OK-only targets
recommendation.body: Add a narrow `channels.whatsapp.heartbeat.targets` style contract for visible OK acknowledgments only, with account/allowlist validation and unchanged alert routing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties steipete to WhatsApp schema sharing, outbound target resolution, and the prior review discussion, making him the best available owner for the product contract choice.
